saturation_note: Korean IS saturated for the thing that matters, and the GAP-1 hypothesis is mostly DISCONFIRMED. Thirteen Korean-language queries across seven distinct angles (large-format signage, ESL, art frames, meeting-room nameplates, bus-stop terminals, listed-company/manufacturing, and rental/installation/solution-provider) converged on the same three domestic manufacturers -- Samsung, LG and SOLUM -- all of which the survey already had. There is no hidden Korean manufacturer tier at >=13in. What DOES exist, exactly as predicted, is a domestic RESELLER/INTEGRATOR tier (명윤시스템/MyungYun System, V.PIXXEL, 아이에스솔루션/I-S Solution, mediaviewsu), and a domestic ESL tier that is entirely sub-13in (Rainus/InforTab, Partron ESL, TJ ST, Grittis, Vertexid). That tier is a long tail of small SIs and cannot be exhaustively enumerated, but it is commercially uninteresting here: they resell Samsung/LG/SOLUM boxes at Korean list price and add no integration capability. Two genuine Korean-specific outputs justify the sweep: (1) a real Korean street price for the Samsung 32in (KRW 1,710,000 vs KRW 2,390,000 list), and (2) ADLAB, a Taiwanese maker with four >=13in models, which surfaced ONLY through its Korean-language site and had been missed by the English/Chinese/Japanese sweeps. Marginal return on further Korean querying is now near zero. Caveat: I could not read Naver's or Danawa's indexes directly (they do not surface to this search tool), so a Korean-only smart-store seller could still be unseen -- but any such seller would be reselling, not manufacturing.
count_basis: Counted over the union of distinct real companies named in `devices` and `vendors` (30 total; the EPIA association entry and the two unattributed ePaper Mall listings are excluded as they are not vendors). The 5 already-known are Samsung, LG, SOLUM, Geniatech and Jiangxi Xingtai/SEEKINK. Additional new names appear in `search_log` but are not profiled -- Korean ESL and reseller tier (Rainus, Partron ESL, TJ ST, Grittis, Vertexid, V.PIXXEL, HL스페이스), E Ink IC partners (Fitipower, Himax, UltraChip, Realtek, IST, Novatek), Sharp, Exeger, Daylight Computer, and ~25 non-display EPIA members in batteries, adhesives, FPC, touch and photovoltaics -- so the true new-name yield is higher than 25 but only 25 met the bar of being plausibly relevant enough to profile.

leads_not_followed.lead: The ~208 EPIA members visible only behind registration. Registration is free-form ([Register] then [Login]) and would unlock /SearchQuery with PSize paging plus the 72-value advanced-search filter set, including the 'Applcations of large size ePaper' tag that would isolate exactly the target population in one query.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This is now the single highest-value unexplored source in the entire survey, and unlike the rest of the web it is a structured, filterable database with a large-size-ePaper facet built in. Four times more members sit behind the login than in front of it. I did not register because creating an account is an action requiring the owner's consent, not a research technique. Worth an explicit decision.

leads_not_followed.lead: ADLAB's actual image-load mechanism for WYED312L / WYED280L / WYED133C. The spec sheets prove Linux, USB-A host, RJ45 and removable micro-SD system storage, but the update path is entirely undocumented publicly.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: These are the best-shaped candidates found for an offline archive and the only >=13in units with confirmed Ethernet plus USB host plus removable storage. Whether they take a file over the LAN or need a vendor tool is the whole decision. One email to the Taipei office (+886-2-8791-8368) resolves it. Their 28in Android sibling has an explicit SD slot, so a sideloadable variant of the 31.2in may already exist.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the AUO Display Plus AecoPost mobile app accepts arbitrary full-resolution user images, and whether the advertised 'API integration with existing CMS' is available without a commercial IMPRESS contract.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: AecoPost 31.5in Mobile is the best large colour candidate found, and the existence of a separate Cloud SKU strongly implies the Mobile SKU works without any vendor service. If the app takes arbitrary JPEGs over Bluetooth, this is a cloud-free 31.5in Spectra 6 art display available today.

leads_not_followed.lead: Whether the Modos Paper Dev Kit's panel-agnostic FPGA controller can actually drive a 25.3in or 31.5in E Ink panel sourced separately from DKE or E Ink.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: This is the only route found to a LARGE display with a fully open, vendor-independent image path. The dev kit is explicitly described as supporting a range of E Ink panels and the Caster gateware is open source. If it scales past 13.3in it dominates every other option on the openness axis. Requires reading the Caster repository and the panel timing requirements.

leads_not_followed.lead: TPV's 31.2in and 42in black-and-white ePaper signage, reported in secondary coverage but never confirmed against a TPV or E Ink primary page.
leads_not_followed.why_it_matters: 42in would be the largest single-panel e-paper signage anywhere in this survey. TPV is also the manufacturing parent behind the already-known Philips/PPDS brand, so this may be the industrial origin of a product the survey already holds under another name -- a possible duplicate worth resolving.

leads_not_followed.lead: Suzhou Etag's 'ePaper industrial flat panel' product, and Ink Cubic's corporate identity.
